page: Amazon Web Services c5.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8124M processor operating at a base clock frequency of 3.4 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware resources include 4 vCPUs mapped across 2 dedicated physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is provisioned at 8.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, delivering 2.0 GB per vCPU. The processor provides 24 MB of L3 cache alongside support for AVX-512 vector extensions and hardware-accelerated AES encryption. Local instance storage is not included, requiring network-attached storage volumes, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 1 Gbps with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses and no dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark metrics reflect moderate single-thread compute capabilities coupled with resource constraints under multi-threaded loads. Single-core evaluations show standard generational throughput, with Geekbench single-core registering 1157.0 points and stress-ng single-core scoring 1493.19. Single-threaded data handling tests such as gzip compression reached 24.06 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression achieved 9.1 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics rank lower across aggregate evaluations, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 2536.0, Clang software compilation at 3457.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 4592.75. Memory bandwidth yields 26.42 GB/sec for uncached reads and 23.29 GB/sec for writes, resulting in a lower-tier PassMark memory index of 1078.56.

From an architectural standpoint, the 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio prioritizes dedicated CPU processing over memory-dense caching. The absence of built-in storage shifts all I/O workloads to external block storage over the 1 Gbps network connection. Cost efficiency is defined by steady dedicated CPU cycles without the overhead of excess memory allocations. Amazon Web Services c5.xlarge is suited for moderate compute-bound workloads, batch processing tasks, Clang build runners, microservices, and web servers that do not require high memory footprints or fast local disk operations.
description: Amazon Web Services c5.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro system, featuring a 3.4 GHz Intel Xeon 8124M processor on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps. The instance lacks bundled local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on remote block storage for persistence. In benchmark tests, the instance demonstrates average single-core efficiency with a Geekbench score of 1157.0 and gzip compression of 24.06 GB/sec, while multi-core metrics like the PassMark CPU score of 4592.75 place it in lower percentiles due to its two-core physical count. With an allocation of 2.0 GB RAM per vCPU, it functions effectively for CPU-focused workloads, small-to-midsize batch processing, microservice deployment, and static web serving.
